I need to consider the factual accuracy of these answers about boll weevil damage.

The boll weevil (Anthonomus grandis) is a beetle that feeds specifically on cotton buds and flowers. It has been one of the most destructive pests in the history of cotton agriculture, particularly devastating cotton crops in the southern United States throughout the 20th century. The name "boll" itself refers to the cotton boll (the seed pod of the cotton plant).

Agent 1's answer of "Wheat" is incorrect. Boll weevils do not attack wheat crops.

Agents 2, 3, and 4 all correctly identified "Cotton" as the crop damaged by boll weevils, with very high confidence levels (0.97, 0.97, and 1.00 respectively).

The majority answer is clearly correct based on well-established agricultural and entomological facts
